(a) Findings; public purpose. Based on the experiences of other urban counties, including but not limited to this county, Fulton County, and Richmond County, Georgia; and other urban municipalities, including but not limited to Atlanta and Smyrna, Georgia, Austin, Texas, Los Angeles, California, and Indianapolis, Indiana, which experiences are relevant to the problems faced by this county; and based on the Austin City Study from Austin, Texas, and other opinions proffered by the county's police department and court personnel, the board of commissioners takes note of the well-known and self-evident conditions attendant to the commercial exploitation of human sexuality which do not vary greatly among generally comparable communities within our country.
(1) It is the finding of the board of commissioners that public nudity (either partial or total) under certain circumstances, particularly circumstances related to the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages in so-called "nude bars" or establishments offering so-called "nude entertainment" or "adult entertainment," leads to an increase in criminal activity, and economic blight and diminution in property values of the surrounding areas.
(2) Among the acts of criminal activity behavior identified with the commercial combination of live nudity and alcohol are disorderly conduct, prostitution, solicitation, drug trafficking, drug use and corruption of public officials. Among the undesirable community conditions identified with the commercial combination of live nudity and alcohol are depression of property values and acceleration of community blight in the surrounding neighborhood, increased allocation of and expenditure for law enforcement personnel to preserve law and order, and increased burden on the judicial system as a consequence of the criminal behavior hereinabove described.
(3) Accordingly, it is in the best interests of the health, welfare, safety and morals of the community to reduce the adverse impact of adult entertainment establishments by limiting the number of such uses, so as to reduce the negative impacts of adult entertainment establishments upon other business uses, neighborhood property values, residential areas and public and semipublic uses, to insure that adult entertainment establishments do not impede development, redevelopment and neighborhood revitalization efforts.
(4) The purpose of this section is to prohibit certain types of attire, conduct and activity in the form of adult entertainment within establishments licensed to serve alcoholic beverages, to the end that the many types of criminal activities frequently engendered by such businesses will be curtailed. However, it is recognized that the prohibition of adult entertainment cannot de facto be inclusive, otherwise a protected form of expression would vanish. As to establishments serving alcoholic beverages and offering adult entertainment, this section represents a balancing of competing interests: reduced criminal activity and protection of the neighborhoods through the prohibition of adult entertainment in establishments licensed to sell alcoholic beverages versus the protected rights of adult entertainment establishments and patrons.
Therefore, the prohibition of adult entertainment in establishments licensed to sell alcoholic beverages is in the public welfare and is a matter of governmental interest and concern to minimize the occurrence of criminal behavior and undesirable community conditions normally associated with establishments which serve alcoholic beverages and provide adult entertainment. To that end, this section is hereby adopted.

564:

Authorized catered function means an authorized catered function as that term is defined and used in O.C.G.A. § 3-11-2 et seq.
Director means Director of the Clayton County Community Development Department.
Drink means any distilled spirits beverage served for consumption on the premises, which may or may not be diluted by any other liquid.
Food caterer shall mean any person who prepares food for consumption off the premises and has a license to do so.
Licensed alcoholic beverage caterer shall mean any retail dealer who has been licensed pursuant to the provisions of this chapter and O.C.G.A. § 3-11-2.
Licensed alcoholic beverage caterer/concessionaire shall mean any retail dealer who has been licensed pursuant to the provisions of this chapter, and is under contract with Clayton County to provide caterer/concessionaire services exclusively at the Clayton County International Park.
Licensee shall mean the person to whom a license is issued, or in the case of a partnership or corporation, all partners, officers, and directors of such partnership or corporation.
Package means a bottle, can, keg, barrel, or other original consumer container.
Purchase price means the consideration received for the sale of alcoholic beverages by the drink valued in money, whether received in cash or otherwise, including all receipts, cash, credits, and property or services of any kind or nature, and also the amount for which credit is allowed by the licensee to the purchaser, without any deduction therefrom whatsoever.
Purchaser means any person who orders and gives present or future consideration for any alcoholic beverage by the drink.
Special event means an event or function as that term is defined and used in chapter 22, article X of Code Of Clayton County, Georgia, as well as an authorized catered function, as defined above.
(Ord. No. 2003-33, §§ 1, 2, 3-18-03)
565:
Alcoholic beverage caterers may operate in the county only under a license granted by the county on the terms and conditions provided in this article. Wine, beer and malt beverages, and distilled spirits shall not be distributed, sold or possessed for the purposes of sale without a license granted by the county. A separate application must be made and a separate alcoholic beverage caterer license must be obtained for each place of business.
(Ord. No. 2003-33, §§ 1, 2, 3-18-03)
566:
(a) Any holder of a county license authorizing the licensee to sell beer, malt beverages, or wine by the drink for consumption on the premises may apply for an off premises license as an alcoholic beverage caterer to sell or distribute beer, malt beverages, or wine by the drink off premises and in connection with an authorized catered function or "special event," and at the location of that function or "special event."
(b) Any holder of a county license authorizing the licensee to sell beer, malt beverages, or wine by the package for consumption off the premises may apply for an off premises license as an alcoholic beverage caterer to sell or distribute beer, malt beverages, or wine by the drink off premises and in connection with an authorized catered function or "special event," and at the location of that function or "special event."
(c) Any holder of a county license authorizing the licensee to sell distilled spirits by the drink for consumption on the premises may apply for an off premises license as an alcoholic beverage caterer to sell or distribute distilled spirits by the drink off premises and in connection with an authorized catered function or "special event," and at the location of that function or "special event."
(d) Any holder of a county license authorizing the licensee to sell distilled spirits by the package for consumption off the premises may apply for an off premises license as an alcoholic beverage caterer to sell or distribute beer, malt beverages, or wine by the drink off premises and in connection with an authorized catered function or "special event," and at the location of that function or "special event."
(e) Each application for a license as an alcoholic beverage caterer shall be accompanied by a certified check for the full amount of the license fee, as follows:
(1) Alcoholic beverage caterers selling wine to be consumed on the premises of and at the location of the function or "special event," $100.00 per year.
(2) Alcoholic beverage caterers selling beer and malt beverages to be consumed on the premises of and at the location of the function or "special event," $100.00 per year.
(3) Alcoholic beverage caterers selling distilled spirits to be consumed on the premises of and at the location of the function or "special event," $200.00 per year.
(4) A combination license for alcoholic beverage caterers selling wine and beer and malt beverages to be consumed on the premises of and at the location of the function or "special event," $150.00 per year.
(5) A combination license for alcoholic beverage caterers selling wine, beer and malt beverages and distilled spirits to be consumed on the premises of and at the location of the function or "special event," $250.00 per year.
(Ord. No. 2003-33, §§ 1, 2, 3-18-03)
567:
(a) Any alcoholic beverage caterer who possesses a valid license from Clayton County or another county or city in Georgia and possesses a valid license from the State of Georgia to sell malt beverages, wine, or distilled spirits by the drink or by the package at a fixed location within the county may be issued by the county an event permit authorizing such sales off premises and in connection with an authorized catered event or function or "special event," and at the location of that function or "special event."
(b) A licensed alcoholic beverage caterer may sell only that beverage which is authorized by the alcoholic beverage license in effect. For example, if the alcoholic beverage caterer possesses a valid license to sell malt beverages, only malt beverages can be sold by the alcoholic beverage caterer at an authorized catered event or function or "special event."
(c) Any food caterer, as defined herein, operating within the county shall apply for an alcoholic beverage caterer's license in order to distribute or sell any distilled spirits, beer, malt beverages or wine off the premises of the food caterer's business. This does not effect any requirements that the food caterer have a license to sell alcoholic beverages on the premises of the food caterer's business.
(d) An alcoholic beverage caterer shall submit an application for an off premises event permit to the director. The license may be applied for at the same time as the alcoholic beverages license(s).
(e) It is unlawful for any person to engage in, carry on or conduct the sale or distribution of alcoholic beverages off premises and in connection with an authorized catered event or function or "special event" without first having obtained a permit as provided herein.
(Ord. No. 2003-33, §§ 1, 2, 3-18-03)
568:
(a) Exclusive of the license required herein, each alcoholic beverage caterer wishing to sell or distribute distilled spirits, beer, malt beverages, or wine at an authorized catered event or function or "special event" within the county must apply for an event permit. The application for the event shall include the name of the caterer and the alcoholic beverage caterer's license number; the date, location, time and name of the event; and the quantity of alcoholic beverages to be transported from the licensee's primary location to the location of the authorized catered event or function or "special event."
(b) When an alcoholic beverage caterer is domiciled outside Clayton County and is currently licensed by the local government authority in which it is domiciled as an alcoholic beverage caterer, a county license shall not be required in order for the alcoholic beverage caterer to distribute or sell distilled spirits, malt beverages, or wine at an authorized catered function or "special event" inside the county. However, there shall be an event permit fee of $100.00 charged by the county and each application for an event permit as an alcoholic beverage caterer shall be accompanied by a certified check for the full amount of the event permit fee. In addition, taxes shall be levied on the total quantity of alcoholic beverages brought into the county by the caterer and they shall be levied and paid in full with the application for an event permit. A copy of the license issued by the local government authority where the alcoholic beverage caterer is domiciled shall be attached to the event application.
(c) The event permit fee shall be $50.00 for those caterers located inside the county. Each application for an event permit as an alcoholic beverage caterer shall be accompanied by a certified check for the full amount of the event permit fee.
(d) The original event permit shall be kept in the vehicle at all times while transporting the alcoholic beverages to the authorized catered event or function or "special event;" it also shall be maintained at the site of the catered event and available for inspection at the event or function during the duration of such event or function or "special event."
(e) It is unlawful for a licensed alcoholic beverage caterer to distribute or sell alcoholic beverages off premises, except as authorized by the event permit.
(f) The event permit will be valid for the length of the authorized catered event or function or "special event" or as approved by Clayton County. After expiration of the event, the alcoholic beverage caterer shall apply for a new event permit in the same manner as the original permit.
(Ord. No. 2003-33, §§ 1, 2, 3-18-03)
569:
An alcoholic beverage caterer/concessionaire may operate only at the Clayton County International Park (the "park"), and only under licenses granted by the county on the terms and conditions provided in this article. Wine, beer and malt beverages, and distilled spirits shall not be distributed, sold or possessed for the purposes of sale at the park without (i) an alcoholic retail consumption dealer license granted by the county, (ii) an alcoholic beverage caterer/concessionaire license granted by the county, and (iii) an alcoholic retail consumption dealer license granted by the state.
(Ord. No. 2003-33, §§ 1, 2, 3-18-03)
570:
(a) The holder of a county license alcohol retail consumption dealer license authorizing the licensee to sell beer, malt beverages, wine, or distilled spirits by the drink for consumption may apply for an license as an alcoholic beverage caterer/concessionaire to sell or distribute beer, malt beverages, wine, or distilled spirits by the drink for consumption only at the park and in connection with an authorized catered/concession function taking place thereon.
(b) The combined license fee for an alcohol retail consumption dealer license to be used in conjunction with the license to operate as an alcoholic beverage caterer/concessionaire shall be $1,500.00. In the event the applicant possesses an alcohol retail consumption dealer license for a location other than the park, the license fee for an alcoholic beverage caterer/concessionaire license shall be $500.00.
(Ord. No. 2003-33, §§ 1, 2, 3-18-03)
571:
Any license issued hereunder shall automatically expire on December 31st of the year of its issuance. Each licensee shall make a written application for renewal on or before November 15th of each year.
(Ord. No. 2003-33, §§ 1, 2, 3-18-03)
572:
(a) No person under the age of 21 shall be employed by a licensed alcoholic beverage caterer, who, in the course of such employment, would dispense, serve, sell, or handle alcoholic beverages as prohibited by O.C.G.A. § 3-3-23.
(b) No alcoholic beverage caterer may distribute or sell alcoholic beverages during any hours prohibited in the state or county or on any days prohibited in the state or county.
(Ord. No. 2003-33, §§ 1, 2, 3-18-03)
573:
Any person violating any provision of this chapter shall be guilty of an ordinance violation, and be subject to a fine of up to $1,000.00 and/or six months in jail per violation. Additionally, any person violating this chapter may, after a hearing as provided under the licensee's malt beverage and wine and/or distilled spirits license(s), have the license(s) suspended or revoked and/or be subject to other penalties as provided for in connection with violations of said license(s).
(Ord. No. 2003-33, §§ 1, 2, 3-18-03; Ord. No. 03-128, § 3, 9-16-03)

579:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Amusement machine means any machine or device used or operated by a person for the purpose of receiving its temporary services for the pleasure, recreation, amusement or enjoyment of the operator, which term includes, but is not limited to, billiard or pool tables, pinball machines, electronic video game machines and other similar devices. This term does not include "vending machines" whose operation is not intended to further the pleasure, recreation, amusement or enjoyment of the operator.
Class B coin operated amusement machine means a bona fide coin operated amusement machine that rewards a successful player with any combination of the following items:
(1) Merchandise limited to noncash merchandise, prizes, toys, gift certificates, or novelties, each of which has a wholesale value of not more than $5.00 received for a single play of the game or device.
(2) Points, tokens, vouchers, tickets, or other evidence of winnings which may be exchanged for free replays or rewards set forth in subsection (i) of this definition.
Distributor means any person which sets up for operation by another, or which leases or rents for the purpose of operation by another, any amusement machine, whether such payment for leasing or renting is based upon a fixed charge or rental, upon the basis of a division of the income derived from such amusement machine or upon any other form or method of payment.
Proprietor means any person who, as owner or lessee in possession, has control of the business establishment, place or premises in which any amusement machine is placed for operation, or kept for use or play, or is on exhibition for the purposes of use or play by the general public.
(Code 1973, § 2-16-99; Ord. No. 2010-247, § 1, 12-14-10)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
580:
No person shall engage in the business of being a distributor or proprietor of amusement machines without first obtaining a license for each calendar year.
(Code 1973, § 2-16-100)
581:
The license fee for each distributor or proprietor shall be based upon the total gross receipts provided in chapter 22, derived from the operation of the amusement machines. The licensee shall pay such fee each year, in advance, and is subject to all rules and regulations not in conflict with this article as more fully set forth in this article.
(Code 1973, § 2-16-101)
582:
All applications, original, amended or renewal, for a license under this article shall be filed in writing with the department of community development on a form provided by the department, which shall specify the following:
(1) Applicant's name and address, and if a firm, corporation, partnership or association, the principal owners, officers or partners thereof and their addresses.
(2) The street address of the premises where the amusement machines are to be operated and a description of the general character of all business activities carried on within such premises.
(3) The number and description of amusement machines to be operated upon the business premises.
(4) The name and address of the owner of each amusement machine, if other than the distributor or proprietor of the business applying for the license.
(Code 1973, § 2-16-102)
583:
Any license issued under this article shall be issued in the name of the legal owner of the business and shall be posted in a conspicuous place upon the business premises. Any such license shall be nonassignable and nontransferable from one location to another, but shall apply only to the specific business premises location for which such license is issued. A processing fee of $25.00 shall be assessed for each original, amended or renewal application, which fee shall be tendered by the applicant at the time the application is submitted. Upon approval of the initial, amended or renewal application by the department of community development, the proper license fee shall be tendered for all amusement machines to be operated upon the premises and the department shall issue the appropriate license.
(Code 1973, § 2-16-103)
584:
If any licensee under this article, after the expiration of any portion of any license year, desires to increase the number of amusement machines to be used or played or exhibited for use or play in the establishment, an amended application shall be filed to reflect the information required in section 10-30. Payment of the appropriate license fee applicable to the machines added shall be tendered with the amended application.
(Code 1973, § 2-16-104)
585:
All licensees licensed under this article shall be subject to the following regulations:
(1) Alcoholic beverages shall not be brought onto the premises by patrons of the business, notwithstanding the fact that the licensee may also be licensed to sell alcohol on the premises.
(2) The county's sheriff, police or any other duly constituted law enforcement officer or administrative enforcement official shall be authorized to inspect the licensee's premises during normal business hours for the purpose of determining whether the provisions of this article are being obeyed. All suspected violations shall be reported promptly to the appropriate prosecuting or administrative authorities of the county, including the director of the department of permits and licenses. All information and assistance shall be rendered by such inspecting officer or official as is necessary for the proper enforcement of this article or any state or federal law, either civil or criminal.
(Code 1973, § 2-16-105)
589:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Premises, in addition to the building and any curtilage normally considered as appurtenant thereto, means all public and private parking areas adjacent to the building on the same parcel, regardless of size.
Teen lounge means any business establishment, either for-profit or non-profit, catering exclusively to individuals between the ages of 13 to 17 years and which is operated primarily as a place for such individuals to congregate for social or educational activities for an admission fee. Patrons must present a picture identification for admission into the establishment. A teen lounge shall not include any business establishment which is operated as a place for the exchange of merchandise for consideration.
(Code 1973, § 2-4-41; Ord. No. 2019-97, § 2, 8-20-19)
Cross reference— Definitions generally, § 1-2.
590:
(a) Every person keeping, operating or maintaining a teen lounge within the unincorporated area of the county for use by the public shall be required to obtain a license from the department of community development on a form to be provided by the county in the manner specified in this article and upon approval, based upon adequate assurance that the operating provision contained in this article can be met.
(b) No licensee shall have been convicted nor have entered a plea of nolo contendere within the ten years immediately preceding the date of application for any felony or crime involving moral turpitude. In those instances involving corporations, this prohibition shall also apply to the corporation's president, vice-president, secretary, treasurer and all stockholders owning 20 percent or more of the corporation's stock.
(c) It shall be the duty of all licensees to file with the department of community development the names of all employees with their home addresses, home telephone numbers and places of employment. Changes in the list of employees, with the names of new employees, must be filed with the department within three days from the date of any such change. All employees shall be subject to such investigation rules and regulations as may be deemed necessary from time to time by the department of community development. A $20.00 investigation fee shall be paid by all licensees for each employee.
(Code 1973, § 2-4-40; Ord. No. 2019-97, § 3, 8-20-19)
